## HIGH-priority finding details

### H-1: Dispatch-breaker "Parked issues" panel and its API undocumented  (3/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` told readers a parked issue "stays parked until a person clears it" but never said how; `reference/admin-ui.mdx`'s Runners section and Admin API table omitted the mechanism entirely.
- **Source**: `src/dispatch-breaker.ts` parks an issue+phase after `DISPATCH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` consecutive dispatch failures; `src/index.ts:481` gates dispatch selection on the parked state; `src/admin-ui/pages/runners.ts:16-25,123-217,310` renders a live "Parked issues" section with an Unpark button; `src/admin.ts:385-410` serves `GET /api/parked` and `POST /api/parked/unpark`.
- **Edit**: Added a "Parked issues" subsection to the Runners panel, the two endpoints to the Admin API reference, and linked `DISPATCH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD` to it — selected from run-3 of 3 candidates.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in all runs.

### H-2: "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" wrongly required  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `quickstart.mdx`, `setup/github-app.mdx`, and `setup/target-repo.mdx` each told the reader to enable this target-repo toggle, warning that PR creation or the implementation workflow would otherwise fail.
- **Source**: `ai-implement/CLAUDE.md:179` states the toggle only governs the default `github-actions[bot]` actor, while every synced workflow opens PRs with a GitHub App installation token — confirmed in `workflows/claude-implement.yml`, which mints and uses an App token for the push/PR step.
- **Edit**: Removed the false instruction from all three pages and added a corrective `<Note>` to `setup/github-app.mdx`'s permissions step — selected from run-3 of 2 candidates for `github-app.mdx`; the other two files' removals were identical between runs.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in both runs that found it.

### H-3: Node.js version prerequisite wrong (20+ vs. exactly 24)  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `setup/prerequisites.mdx` said "Node.js 20 or later" in both a summary card and a dedicated Step.
- **Source**: `package.json:10-12` pins `"node": ">=24 <25"`; `.tool-versions:1` pins `nodejs 24.15.0`; `scripts/check-node-version.mjs:25-39` hard-fails on any other major version, run by `npm run dev`, `dev:local`, and `dev:run` before they start.
- **Edit**: Corrected both mentions to Node.js 24 — selected from run-3 of 2 candidates.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in both runs that found it.

### H-4: `.env` auto-load claim in `deploy.mdx` is reversed  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `setup/deploy.mdx` instructed readers to manually export `.env` variables, claiming the `dev` script has "no dotenv integration."
- **Source**: `package.json:18,20,21` — `dev`, `dev:local`, and `dev:run` all pass `--env-file-if-exists=.env` to `tsx`, auto-loading the file.
- **Edit**: Replaced the manual-export instructions with a one-line confirmation that `.env` loads automatically — selected from run-3 of 2 candidates.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH in both runs that found it.

### H-5: `autoMerge` setting has no effect — grouping-branch merges are unconditional  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Both pages described child-pull-request-into-grouping-branch merging as opt-in per project via the `autoMerge` toggle, off by default.
- **Source**: `auto-merge.ts:36-49`'s `runAutoMerges()` (which checks `mapping.autoMerge`) is defined but never called outside its own file and tests. Only the unconditional `runGroupingBranchAutoMerge()` (`auto-merge.ts:60-73`, called from `index.ts:461`) is wired into the poll loop.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the "Merging child pull requests" section and the `autoMerge` `<ParamField>` to state that grouping-branch merging is unconditional and the field currently has no effect on it.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only one run reached this area).

### H-6: Sibling file-overlap dispatch deferral undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/feature-branch-grouping.mdx`'s "When each issue runs" table listed four situations, omitting this one.
- **Source**: `poll-selection.ts:173-214` (`selectFileOverlapDeferrals`) defers a candidate sibling whose declared `Files:` list overlaps an in-flight sibling's on the same grouping branch, wired via `index.ts:506`.
- **Edit**: Added a table row and an explanatory note describing the deferral and its file-declaration source.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only one run reached this area).

### H-7: Stuck-run give-up notification undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/notifications.mdx`'s event list had no entry for this notification.
- **Source**: `stuck-watchdog.ts:9,25-88` — after `STUCK_JOB_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (3) failed requeue attempts, `boundedCleanup()` clears the ticket's working state and sends `notifyStuckGiveUp`.
- **Edit**: Added a "Stuck — needs human" bullet to the Run lifecycle list.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only one run reached this area).

### H-8: Dispatch-failure notification undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Only a successful "Dispatch" notification was documented.
- **Source**: `dispatch-failure.ts:26-64` (`surfaceDispatchFailure`) sends a distinct failure notification, including a re-sync hint on HTTP 422.
- **Edit**: Added a "Dispatch failed" bullet describing the failure notification and the 422 hint.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only one run reached this area).

### H-9: Completion status enum missing `review_failed`  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: The Completion bullet listed outcomes as `completed`, `failed`, or `timed_out`.
- **Source**: `notify.ts:36` (`CompletionNotification.status`) and `completionLabel()` (lines 284-298) show a fourth real status, `review_failed`, fired whenever post-push review leaves blockers.
- **Edit**: Added `review_failed` to the enumerated outcomes with a one-line explanation and a link to Post-push review.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only one run reached this area).

### H-10: `skillsRepo` accepts only GitHub, not "a full git URL"  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/team-repo-mappings.mdx` described `skillsRepo` as accepting "an `owner/repo` shorthand or a full git URL."
- **Source**: `src/admin.ts`'s `normalizeSkillsRepo` throws a validation error for anything other than the `owner/repo` shorthand or an `https://github.com/...` URL.
- **Edit**: Narrowed the field description to the two forms actually accepted and added a sentence explaining why other hosts and SSH URLs are rejected.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only one run reached this area).

### H-11: Planning-phase comment format stale; parallel-subagent feature doesn't exist  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `how-it-works.mdx`, `configuration/planning.mdx`, and `customize/planning-md.mdx` all described four planning comments (Architecture Analysis, Test Plan, Work Units, Cross-Story Context) and claimed the implementation phase spins up parallel Claude subagents when a "Work Units" comment is present.
- **Source**: `workflows/PLANNING.md:48-171` — the current template writes exactly three comments (Implementation Map, Acceptance Bar, Risks & Open Questions); cross-story notes fold into the Implementation Map. `src/pipeline/steps/implement.ts:17,52` shows `subagentCount` is hardcoded to `0` and never set elsewhere — the parallel-subagent behavior does not exist in this version.
- **Edit**: Rewrote the comment-type sections on all three pages to the current three comments and removed the parallel-subagent claim.
- **Priority agreement**: HIGH (only one run reached this area).

## MEDIUM-priority finding details

### M-1: Self-deploy (`FLY_DEPLOY_TOKEN`) undocumented  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Neither `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` nor `setup/deploy.mdx` mentions `FLY_DEPLOY_TOKEN` or the self-deploy feature, despite `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` billing itself as covering every startup variable.
- **Source**: `index.ts:226` reads `FLY_DEPLOY_TOKEN`; `deploy.ts:418-420` (`canSelfDeploy`) gates the feature on it plus the `AI_IMPLEMENT_SOURCE_*` build-stamp vars; `.env.example:188,193-195` lists all four.

### M-2: `KG_SIDECAR_URL` / `KG_SOURCE_REPO` undocumented  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: Neither variable appears on `configuration/environment-variables.mdx`, though the MCP server section documents variables that depend on them.
- **Source**: `index.ts:242` reads `KG_SOURCE_REPO`; `.env.example:142-151` documents both, noting `KG_SIDECAR_URL` unset degrades `/mcp` to an indistinguishable `401`.

### M-3: "bd-belay-on is the only skill with no ticketing dependency" is false  (2/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/introduction.mdx`'s Ticketing support note names `bd-belay-on` as the sole exception.
- **Source**: `bd-system-questions/SKILL.md` and `bd-kg-search/SKILL.md` contain no ticketing-tracker references either — the same zero-dependency profile as `bd-belay-on`.

### M-4: Admin API reference omits deploy endpoints  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/admin-ui.mdx`'s "Admin API reference" table, presented as a full endpoint list, omits the Deployments panel's endpoints.
- **Source**: `admin.ts:235,240,263` register `POST /api/deploy`, `GET /api/deployment-status`, and `POST /api/deploy-policy`.

### M-5: `AI_IMPLEMENT_LOG_LEVEL=stream` phrasing implies tool output is logged  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` says stream mode logs "each tool call with a summary of its input, each result, and any text it writes."
- **Source**: `claude-stream.ts:170-179`'s `formatEvent()` prints only the literal string `"[claude] tool_result"` for a tool result — never the actual output content.

### M-6: Closing a roll-up PR unmerged is a permanent, silent veto  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/feature-branch-grouping.mdx`'s "Rolling completed work back up" section only describes the merge path.
- **Source**: `merge-up.ts:155-167` — once the top-of-tree PR is closed unmerged, the orchestrator logs it once and skips that tree forever; nothing reopens or recreates the PR.

### M-7: Linear auto-transitions workflow state, not just labels  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/labels.mdx`'s Linear tab documents only label add/remove behavior.
- **Source**: `providers/linear.ts:672-735` (`transitionToInProgressIfMovable`) also moves the issue's Linear workflow state to "In Progress" when eligible.

### M-8: Reaper burst-alert notification undocumented  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/notifications.mdx` has no mention of this notification.
- **Source**: `reaper.ts:260-270` sends `notifyReaperBurst` when a sweep destroys more machines than `REAPER_ALERT_THRESHOLD` (default 10).

### M-9: "Deployment available" notice undocumented; gating claim overstated  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/notifications.mdx`'s "Deploy notifications" section documents only the shutdown/deployed/restarted trio, and states these notices are sent "only where the orchestrator can identify its own image, which in practice means Fly.io."
- **Source**: `deploy-notify.ts:202-221` (`postAvailableNotice`) is a fourth deploy-notification kind, and its own comment states it deliberately does not gate on `FLY_IMAGE_REF`.

### M-10: Completion notification's remediation content under-described  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: The Completion bullet says the message includes only outcome, PR link, run link, and duration.
- **Source**: `notify.ts:315-354,356-432` also append a classification summary, detail, a "Next step" remediation, and a Troubleshooting-guide link sourced from `completion-classification.ts:19-59` (`classifyCompletion`).

### M-11: Error-codes table missing `machine_max_age_sweep` timeout reason  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `reference/error-codes.mdx`'s timeout-reason table lists `container_timeout`, `machine_timeout`, `run_not_found`, `timed_out`.
- **Source**: `reaper.ts:222` sets conclusion `machine_max_age_sweep` on a sweep-triggered timeout, turned by `completion-classification.ts:34-39` into a user-visible message shown in both the ticket comment and the completion notification.

### M-12: `bd-high-plan`'s dedicated Jira handling missing from enumeration  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/introduction.mdx` names only `bd-build-up`, `bd-mega-build-up`, and `bd-build-down` as carrying dedicated Jira handling.
- **Source**: `bd-high-plan/SKILL.md:139-151`'s "Tracker Notes" section gives explicit, distinct Linear vs. Jira filing instructions.

### M-13: Marketplace catalog ref pinned to `v1.0.0`, four releases behind current  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/installation.mdx` states the stable-channel catalog "pins that to the release tag."
- **Source**: At this v1.4.0-tagged checkout, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:13`'s `source.ref` for the `builddown` plugin is still `"v1.0.0"`, while `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:3` is `"1.4.0"`.

### M-14: `--codex` install claim contradicts script's own restart message  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/installation.mdx` says Codex installs require restarting Codex "rather than running `/skills`."
- **Source**: `install.sh:90` sets Codex's own restart message to offer "Restart Codex (or start a new CLI session and run /skills)" as an explicit alternative.

### M-15: Releases page has no entry for the pinned v1.1.0  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `releases.mdx` lists only `v1.0.0` as a release.
- **Source**: This run's `.audit-refs` pins the `ai-implement` checkout to `v1.1.0`, confirming a release shipped after `v1.0.0` with no corresponding changelog entry. Compiling the entry needs the full v1.1.0 changeset, which is outside a single source-to-docs comparison — flagged for the release-notes owner to fill in.

### M-16: Skills `releases.mdx` overstates "story points are gone"  (1/3 runs)
- **Docs**: `skills/releases.mdx`'s v1.4.0 entry states flatly, "Story points are gone."
- **Source**: `bd-summit-push/SKILL.md:277,332,450` — the Push Manifest template still reports `{points} story points`, and two later steps instruct preserving the `estimate` field. The claim holds for `bd-build-up`'s planning output but not for `bd-summit-push`'s own vocabulary.

## Synthesis decisions log (audit-trail for reviewers)

### H-1
- **Present in:** Run 1 HIGH, Run 2 HIGH, Run 3 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** All three cite the same dispatch-breaker parking mechanism and the same undocumented `GET /api/parked` / `POST /api/parked/unpark` endpoints, targeting the same two docs files.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 3
- **Selection reasoning:** Run 3 adds a dedicated `#### Parked issues` subsection to `reference/admin-ui.mdx`, matching the page's existing pattern for sub-features (e.g. "Per-team secrets" / "Global secrets" under Secrets), and its `configuration/environment-variables.mdx` edit links directly to that subsection's anchor (`#parked-issues`). Run 1 and Run 2 both describe the panel inline within the existing "Runners" prose without a dedicated anchor, which would leave Run 3's more precise cross-link broken if paired with either. Run 3's Admin API table rows also drop an internal JSON-body citation that Run 1's included, matching the terser style already used by every other row in that table.

**Edit candidates compared:**

Run 1's approach (not selected) — `reference/admin-ui.mdx`:
```mdx
A **Parked issues** table appears on this panel whenever at least one issue is parked. An issue lands here after [`DISPATCH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD`](...) consecutive dispatch failures for the same issue and phase, and the orchestrator stops picking it up.

Each row shows the issue, repo, phase, failure count, last conclusion, and how long ago it was parked, with an Unpark action. Unparking clears the parked state and resets the failure count to zero for every phase of that issue, so it re-enters normal polling — two failures right after unparking won't re-park it; the full threshold has to be reached again from zero.
```

Run 3's approach (selected) — `reference/admin-ui.mdx`:
```mdx
#### Parked issues

A **Parked issues** section appears on this panel whenever the dispatch circuit breaker has parked at least one issue — after [`DISPATCH_BREAKER_THRESHOLD`](...) consecutive dispatch failures for the same issue and phase, the orchestrator stops picking it up.

Each row shows the issue, repo, phase, failure count, last failure conclusion, and how long ago it was parked. A parked issue stays parked until you **unpark** it from this panel — the breaker never clears one on its own.
```

### H-2
- **Present in:** Run 2 HIGH, Run 3 HIGH
- **Dedup reasoning:** Both cite the same `ai-implement/CLAUDE.md` statement that the GHA "create and approve pull requests" toggle has no effect on App-authenticated workflows, and both target the same three docs pages.
- **Selected edit from:** Run 3 for `setup/github-app.mdx`; Run 2 and Run 3 produced byte-identical edits for `setup/target-repo.mdx` and `quickstart.mdx` (both simply delete the false instruction with no replacement), so no selection was needed for those two files.
- **Selection reasoning:** For `setup/github-app.mdx`, Run 2 adds a new "## Pull request creation needs no extra repo setting" section; Run 3 instead adds an inline `<Note>` inside the existing "Set repository permissions" step, right where the reader actually sets the Pull Requests permission. `CLAUDE.md`'s guidance is to keep a fact at its point of action rather than a separate location, and since the false "point of consequence" section is being deleted outright (not merely trimmed), there is no remaining reason to keep a separate section — Run 3's placement matches this more directly.

**Edit candidates compared:**

Run 2's approach (not selected) — `setup/github-app.mdx`:
```mdx
## Pull request creation needs no extra repo setting

AI-Implement opens every pull request with a token minted from the GitHub App you just created, not the default `github-actions[bot]` actor. Because of that, the target repo's **Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests** toggle (under **Settings → Actions → General**) has no effect on AI-Implement's runs.

<Note>
  Leaving that toggle at its default is harmless — it only governs the separate `github-actions[bot]` identity, which AI-Implement's workflows never use. The permissions that actually matter are the ones you set on the App itself, above.
</Note>
```

Run 3's approach (selected) — `setup/github-app.mdx`:
```mdx
<Note>
  The **Pull requests** permission above is what lets AI-Implement open PRs — every synced workflow authenticates as the App, not as the default `github-actions[bot]` actor. You do not also need to enable target repos' **"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests"** setting; that setting governs the default actor only and has no effect on App-authenticated workflows.
</Note>
```
